brand.name: Dual Orbit
brand.tagline: Data engineering, analysis, and systems that move work forward.
brand.description: Dual Orbit is a capability portfolio for data engineering, data analysis, and system development, presented as runnable proof rather than as a project gallery.

hero.title: Dual Orbit
hero.lede: Three engineering practices presented as capability: data that can be trusted, analysis that answers a real question, and software that people can actually use.
notes: Every interactive data demo on this page was rebuilt from scratch and runs on invented records.
System work is listed with its honest status, from live deployments through to internal work.

capabilities.heading: Capabilities
capabilities.lede: Each practice is described by the problem classes it takes on and the methods it applies.

items.title: Data Engineering
items.summary: Builds one dependable dataset out of sources that disagree, arrive late, and change without warning.
problems: Operational sources that drift apart between databases, files, and hand-maintained sheets.
Repeatable ingestion that has to survive restarts, reruns, and partial failures.
Validation that catches bad records before a report depends on them.
methods: Reconciliation of heterogeneous sources into a governed master model.
Stepwise transforms: filtering, unit normalisation, joins, and unmatched-row analysis.
Workflow validation, branching, bounded retries, and execution visibility.
Pluggable connectors with configurable validation rules.

items.title: Data Analysis
items.summary: Turns a question into evidence that a reviewer can check, challenge, and act on.
problems: Data that has to be explored interactively before the right question is even clear.
Classification where a knowledge base assists but a person still decides.
Reference material that needs to be searchable rather than buried in documents.
methods: Interactive filtering and aggregation over a bounded, understood dataset.
Operational pattern exploration with detail views behind every aggregate.
Knowledge-assisted classification with confidence thresholds and human review.
Local indexing and ranking over originally authored, curriculum-shaped notes and questions.

items.title: System Development
items.summary: Ships the interface layer: the booking, workflow, ledger, and document tools that a business runs on.
problems: Bookings and schedules that need roles, records, and a clear trail.
Operations that need ledgers, agreements, and reusable modules rather than one-off scripts.
Front-end work that has to stay usable on small screens and offline.
methods: Role-aware workflow interfaces with persisted records.
Modular application families that share a common core and vary per module.
Canvas and interactive front-end work with careful keyboard and touch behaviour.
Offline-first and portable document workflows for constrained environments.

approach.heading: Delivery and confidentiality approach
approach.lede: How the material on this page was produced, and what is deliberately not shown.
paragraphs: Every interactive demo published here was rebuilt from scratch for public viewing. The records inside them are invented: synthetic operational rows, synthetic documents, and original reference notes written for this purpose. No employer file, client dataset, schema, workflow definition, or screenshot is reproduced.

For systems that belong to an organisation other than ours, we can only show what that owner has agreed to show. A public URL is listed where one already exists and publishing is permitted; everything else is described by the status it actually holds today, whether that is a live deployment, a demo shell, work in progress, or internal work.
The intent is practical rather than absolute: keep the demonstration honest, keep the boundary visible, and let the status labels do the work that a marketing claim would otherwise do.

points.title: Clean-room demos
points.body: New code, new fixtures, new domain wording. The technique is reproduced; the material is not.

points.title: Permission-conscious evidence
points.body: Only surfaces that are already public, or that an owner has explicitly agreed to publish, appear as links.

points.title: Honest status labels
points.body: Live deployment, demo shell, in development, and internal are used as they apply, without promotion.
